items.what: The “How strong each tie is” scale on the Kimberly-Clark, Duracell, MISA Imports and Sun Products pages
items.was: The scale said Confirmed meant the company or Costco says so in its own words.
items.now: It now uses the same steps as How we know: Confirmed needs a code on the product that leads to the factory; a company’s own statement makes an answer Documented. No stamp changed.
items.why: The scale’s wording didn’t match our published rules. Found in our site audit the day the pages went live.

items.what: The search title of Costco diapers
items.was: The title said Kirkland diapers cost “From 13¢”, rounding up the lowest price.
items.now: The lowest Kirkland price on the page was 12.5¢ a diaper, so the title now says “Under 13¢”. A whole-cent price still reads “From”.
items.why: Rounding 12.5¢ up made the title name a lowest price that a cheaper size undercut. Found in our site audit.

items.what: The date of one Barton 1792 label approval for Kirkland bourbon
items.was: Our record dated TTB approval 20342001000264 to January 29, 2021, and called it approved.
items.now: The approval was issued December 8, 2020, and TTB now lists it as surrendered. January 29, 2021 is the date TTB's search shows as completed. Barton's three other Kirkland approvals are still approved, so the answer is unchanged.
items.why: We read the date from TTB's search results instead of box 19 of the approval. Found when we started reading every Kirkland approval weekly.

items.what: Motorcraft's date code, on the battery date code decoder
items.was: We said we found no rule from Ford or Motorcraft and showed one how-to article's rule as Reported.
items.now: Ford's distributor manual, on a page effective May 2005, shows a shipping date sticker on the side of the battery reading C-2 and 3-2. The decoder reads both forms as a Maker's rule, with the record's date.
items.why: We missed the manual on the first read; it sits in a warranty PDF, not a consumer page.

items.what: Kirkland Stool Softener, on the Kirkland medicine page
items.was: We said the label file named no company.
items.now: The label says “Distributed by: PL Developments”, so the table names PL Developments as the distributor. That doesn't show who made it. Labels that name no company go from 3 to 2.
items.why: We missed the line on the label when we read it, and found it on a re-read.

items.what: ACDelco's P series, on the battery date code decoder
items.was: We showed the P series as Reported, from a seller's guide.
items.now: ACDelco's warranty sheet, revised February 2015, says the first character is P or S and that P 094N means September 2014. P now reads as a Maker's rule, with the record's date.
items.why: We found ACDelco's own sheet on a later read.

items.what: Deka's letter date code, on the battery date code decoder
items.was: Reported: letter codes for Deka came only from a seller's guide, and the 3/23 ship sticker was the one format we could confirm.
items.now: Maker's rule: Deka's care sheet prints a Shipping Date Code, a month letter that skips I, then a year digit, with L1 as November 2011. The two-digit form such as D24 stays Reported.
items.why: We found Deka's own sheet the day the page went live, while reading its storage guidance.

items.what: Opening line of the store-brand motor oil answer
items.was: For eight others, including Kirkland, Amazon Basics, Meijer, Do It Best and Signature Select, most or all of the oils are licensed to one company: Highline Warren LLC.
items.now: For eight others, including Kirkland, Amazon Basics, Meijer, Do It Best and Signature Select, some or all of the oils are licensed to one company: Highline Warren LLC.
items.why: "Most or all" was too strong for every brand: one of the five Members Mark listings is on Highline Warren's license. The company, the license and the counts were right; the summary wording was not.

items.what: What the proof is, on How We Know
items.was: The proof is always a public record you can open yourself. Every answer rests on records anyone can open.
items.now: The proof is always something you can open yourself, and the stamp says how strong it is. A press report on its own can only earn a Reported stamp.
items.why: Some answers rest on press reports, stamped Reported, so not all proof is a public record.

items.was: Public records only. No rumors, no guesses, no photos as proof.
items.now: Records first. A press report only earns a Reported stamp and is never shown as fact.
items.why: The old wording didn't match the site: we use some press reports, stamped Reported, and we publish a page testing rumors.

items.now: 82 sources, 64 of them primary records. Both figures now come from the sources file.
items.why: Not all our sources are primary records. Some are press reports or other secondary sources.

items.what: Kirkland product count on the homepage
items.now: 76 Kirkland products. The count now comes from the Kirkland data file.
items.why: The number was typed in by hand and fell behind as answers were added.

items.what: Opening line of the Kirkland medicine answer
items.was: We read 47 Costco labels on FDA’s DailyMed.
items.now: We read 47 Costco labels on DailyMed, the US government’s library of drug labels.
items.why: DailyMed is run by the National Library of Medicine, not FDA. The labels, the companies and the counts were right; the name of the publisher was not.

items.what: Who approves corrections, on How We Know and About
items.was: Jeremiah approves every Confirmed stamp, anything that alleges a safety or legal problem, and every correction.
items.now: Same, except corrections: only those that change a maker, a stamp or a named company need approval. Typo, count and broken-link fixes go live without waiting and are logged.
items.why: The page promised more than our practice since 5 November, when smaller fixes stopped waiting for approval. The page now says what we do.

items.what: Who makes Kirkland Signature dog food
items.was: The only public record we'd found was Diamond Pet Foods' 2012 recall notice, so we said we couldn't name who makes today's bags.
items.now: North Dakota's pet food register lists all 12 Kirkland dry dog formulas as Costco's, care of Diamond Pet, renewed December 2025. We added wet food (Saturn Petcare), biscuits (North River Enterprises), jerky (Phelps Industries) and dental chews (Nylabone) from the same register.
items.why: We found a newer public record: the state's pet food register and the label files filed with it.

Label file for North Dakota registration 500055938: Kirkland Signature Nature's Domain Beef Meal & Sweet Potato for dogs (bag printer's proof, June 2021)

items.what: The cold brew line under What we don’t know
items.was: The 2023 recall record covers only four lots, with best-by dates of October 19 to 22, 2023.
items.now: The 2023 recall record covers only the lots it lists: nine lots with best-by dates of October 19 to 27, 2023, 231,071 cases in all.
items.why: FDA’s record lists nine lots (231019 to 231027), not four. The company and the record were right; the lot count and date range were not.
